data.why: A front-loading washer stands cut open in a laundry room; the tennis ball and the muddy shirt follow the water from the tap through the drum, the tub and the pump to the drain. The camera starts close on the spinning drum, steps out to the whole machine as each part is added, and goes close on the pump and its filter where the ball jams.

recurring.what: a tennis ball tossed in with the laundry

ideas.idea: spinning a muddy shirt in a drum is the start of a washer
dry, the mud just tumbles around with a tennis ball
turn the tap: water runs down the hose and fills the drum
the drum is full of holes, so the water pours straight out onto the floor
a sealed tub round the drum holds the water in
the mud comes off, and the tub now traps brown water
a pump drains the brown water away up the hose
the pump sucks in the tennis ball and jams
a filter in front of the pump catches the ball
the pump drains the tub but not the water soaked in the shirt
a fast spin flings that water out through the drum's holes
the clean shirt comes out, and the ball comes back from the filter

chain.shows: dry mud tumbles on the shirt beside the tennis ball
water pours out of the drum's holes onto the floor
the tub fills with brown water around the shirt
chain.stakes: the shirt soaks in its own mud

chain.shows: the tennis ball rides into the pump and it jams, brown water backs up
chain.stakes: the pump stops and the machine cannot drain

chain.shows: the drained shirt stays dark and dripping
chain.stakes: the clothes come out heavy and wet

surprises.claim: A front-loading washer's final spin reaches about 1,200 revolutions per minute.
surprises.search: front load washer max spin speed rpm 1200

surprises.claim: A washer's perforated inner drum sits inside a sealed outer tub that holds the water.
surprises.search: washing machine inner drum perforated outer tub holds water

surprises.claim: Front-loading washers have a drain pump filter that catches coins, socks and small objects before they reach the pump.
surprises.search: washing machine drain pump filter catches coins socks

sentences.text: If you spin a muddy shirt in a drum, you have a washer.
But dry mud just tumbles beside a tennis ball.
So you turn the tap to fill the drum.
But the water pours out through the drum's holes.
So you wrap the drum in a sealed tub.
But the tub traps all that brown water.
So you add a pump that drains it.
But the pump sucks in the ball and jams.
So a filter in front catches the ball.
But the pump cannot reach water in the shirt.
So the drum spins 1,200 times a minute, flinging it out.
Pull out a clean shirt, and grab the ball.
Congratulations, you built a washing machine.
